app-notebook-text.note: Approved 2026-09-21; one step darker 2026-10-05 (#ED0702, 4.534:1 on the app background). Never a fill. Watch against the No-Verdict Rule: a pure red.

app-idea-log-text.note: Approved 2026-10-05, as built. An olive that no longer reads as the yellow. Never a fill.

app-blue.note: Icon stroke of Home and the brand mark only; reads 3.90:1 under a white label, so never a fill.

app-blue-text.note: The filled action fill (white label) and the secondary action outline and label. Approved 2026-10-05; one step darker the same day (#1475DD, 4.547:1 on the app background and under the white label). App blue is the link colour (approved 2026-10-05). Known unresolved: every companion reads about 4.1:1 on app-surface-subtle, a pairing never decided.

display.purpose: The recipe name, once per page, in the headnote.

headline.purpose: The version line under the name; the batch row’s churned date; a later batch’s date.

body.purpose: Headnote prose, method instructions, authored notes. Lead-ins bold within the same size.

section.purpose: Region names and block legends — a true heading weight, not a label.

label.purpose: Table headers and the Sheet's running head. The plain, unweighted sibling of Caption.

caption.purpose: Every caption that labels an input: field captions, batch cell labels (on the Sheet and print), axis names, segmented captions. Uppercase by text-transform so the source stays sentence case. The group cues are no longer captions (see app-cue).

control.purpose: Actionable choices, text controls, segmented options, hint and status sentences.

helper.purpose: A helper sentence beside a caption, never inside it — sentence case, always a sibling of the uppercase caption element.

table.purpose: Ingredient table cells, the graduated rule label, and every binder control’s own text. Tabular numerals. The page default.

figure.purpose: The value beside each graduated rule and the step number. The page’s one heavy element, and it stays in ink.

deviation.purpose: The words under a rule stating its standing against its band; a measured cell’s unit; a step’s purpose and aside in italic.

note.purpose: Written notes, typed or saved: 16px at 1.5 leading, at the 65ch measure. Also the size a recorded figure reads at, and the field size wherever the pointer is coarse.

small-print.purpose: Target chips, basis notes, rule anchors, fat breakdown, plan sub-lines, cross-flags, import errors.

hand.purpose: The maker's own saved words in the App: a tasting's note and problems, a Next time, a version's Why, a batch's notes, an idea. Caveat in sheet pen blue, display only; entry uses the prose-field role. Falls back to the text face in italic under forced colours and in print. The Sheet's own hand (.sheet-hand) is Caveat at the hand's minimum with leading 1, for batch edits only.

app-brand.purpose: The wordmark, a link to Home at every width.

app-title.purpose: A list page's title (Home, an unbuilt place).

app-lead-name.purpose: The Home lead block's recipe name and the Notebook band's recipe name.

app-name.purpose: A recipe's name on a Home row.

app-identity.purpose: The version identity heading in the Notebook version column.

app-body.purpose: The recipe description, the Notebook's fields, the log's date and notes.

app-meta.purpose: Version and mass line, nav words, standing words and actions (600), the upright list's titles, History's names.

app-cue.purpose: The record pen's and reading view's group headings (Every recipe, This recipe only): a face of their own so a group never reads as one more item (sketch 011 decisions 40 C and 58 B2).

app-label.purpose: A row's place name, the micro-labels, a field's caption, fold captions, cell labels (600 there), counts (not uppercase).

app-log-value.purpose: A measured cell's figure in the batch log, in the App text colour.

rules.purpose: Stroke weights for the graduated rule, the table, the strike and the drawn controls, and the App's hairline. Depth is rule weight; nothing else conveys it on the Sheet. Hover and focus carry their own 2px weight because 1.5px renders as 1px at DPR 1. The App's hairline (--app-rule-row) is 1px; the History mark's hollow border and the tally's edge are 1.5px and 2px.

focus.color: var(--sheet-ink) on the Sheet and var(--app-text) in the shell (the same value)
focus.exception: .is-landing-focus:focus — a plain :focus rule for the fork’s landing focus after a mouse-driven Save, which Chrome’s modality tracking would otherwise leave ringless. The one documented exception.
focus.purpose: The one focus treatment, provably heavier than the 1px outline pointed-at content carries and a different sign from a picked control's fill. Never colour, never position. The shell's places and menu button read the App text colour; a bottom tab's ring is inset by its own width so it is not drawn off the window.

state.picked: On the Sheet a picked or pressed CONTROL fills pen blue edge to edge, border and all, with paper-coloured text; an independent on/off is a square and a word and only the 13px square fills. In the App's batch log the same fills read app blue's text companion with a white label, because pen blue in the App is the maker's own words.
state.pointedAt: Content the page is pointing at — a marked table row, the open batch, the current version — reads bold plus a 1px ink outline offset 2px, in place.
state.recorded: On the Sheet anything the maker typed or saved reads pen blue and keeps it after saving; an absence (“not measured”) is ink. In the App the maker's saved observations read in the hand in sheet pen blue; measured values and dates read in the App text colour, and an absence reads secondary text.
state.notInForce: One ink strike at 1.2px — a skipped step, a superseded value, a removed row or step. Beside the replacement where there is room, beneath it for a paragraph.
state.forcedColors: The picked fill survives as a fill, repainted in the system Highlight with HighlightText, so state and focus never collapse into the same outline. A focused picked control switches its ring to CanvasText.
state.current: The current place sits on the subtle surface (1.10:1 against white) and takes weight 600 on the rail and the tab row; the current row in the upright list is bold ink with aria-current, not a link.

shadows.name: flyout
shadows.purpose: The fly-out nav panel's edge (--app-shadow-flyout; sketch 011 decision 33), from 724 to 1589. The only shadow the App draws.

shadows.name: scrim
shadows.purpose: The veil under the fly-out, over the page (--app-scrim): the App text colour at 28%. Not a shadow, a layer.

shadows.name: history-in-view-ring
shadows.purpose: The History mark's in-view ring, drawn as two box-shadow rings. A mark's drawing, not depth.

breakpoints.name: nav-rail
breakpoints.purpose: The 224px rail stands beside the page (224 + 3 x 32 + 920 + 350). Below it the nav is the fly-out, opened from the bar's menu button (sketch 011 decision 33, Mark 2026-10-03).

breakpoints.name: recipe-log-beside
breakpoints.purpose: Recipe route (decision 16). The log sits beside the two-column Sheet at 350 (3 x 32 + 920 + 350). Also the folds' cut (decision 18): open by default from here, closed below, no stored state; the band's rhythm and the axes' stacked arrangement switch here.

breakpoints.name: recipe-sheet-two-columns
breakpoints.purpose: Recipe route. The Sheet's second column holds from here up (2 x 32 + 920); below it one column. From 984 the side column spans the ingredients and Instructions rows and the Instructions row takes the surplus (decision 49 A).

breakpoints.name: recipe-phone-forms
breakpoints.purpose: Recipe route (decision 16). The list-form ingredient table, the 20px page margin, the stacked band, the bottom tab row and the scrolling header arrive together (band side-by-side minimum 660 + 64). The record pen's width-only block and BatchRow's useBelow724 share this cut (decision 28).

breakpoints.name: ingredient-grid-form
breakpoints.purpose: The ingredient table's D3 grid form on screen (decision 31, carried to 724 by decision 32). The column form draws only in print.

breakpoints.name: recipe-content-cap
breakpoints.value: min-width: 1546px main area (a 1546px window with the fly-out, 1770px with the rail)
breakpoints.purpose: Content stops growing at 1482 (Sheet 1100 + 32 + log 350) and centres in the main area.

breakpoints.name: touch
breakpoints.purpose: Touch sizes follow the pointer only. Buttons, selects, ink fields, prose fields, segmented options, defect toggles and text controls take a 44px minimum height; an axis stop grows in HEIGHT only, to 38x44; .ink-field and .prose-field read 16px. A narrow mouse window keeps mouse sizes; a real touch device is caught however wide it is.

breakpoints.name: wide-touch
breakpoints.purpose: A tablet held in the hand at a desktop width (sketch 009). Axis and segmented caption lines reserve two lines of caption height so they sit level with the field captions beside them, and Clear takes its 44px target as an overflowing ::after hit area so the line box never grows.

breakpoints.name: home-lead-stack
breakpoints.purpose: Home's own cut: the lead block stacks and the rows drop to three columns.

breakpoints.name: home-phone
breakpoints.purpose: Home's own cut: the row stacks; the rail, the tally and the secondary action go; the filled action fills the row. Home is not on the recipe route's derived ladder yet.

breakpoints.name: forced-colors
breakpoints.purpose: Repaints the picked fill in the system Highlight rather than removing it, and sets the hand back to the text face in italic.

breakpoints.name: print
breakpoints.purpose: The page notice is hidden, the hand falls back to the text face in italic, and the Show changes control on the Ingredients row is hidden. Phase 04 owns the rest of the print layer.

table.purpose: The ingredient table sizes to its content (sketch 011 decision 15). From 724 on screen each row is a grid with named areas (As made, plan amount, name, share), so the plan amount never moves when Show changes toggles (decision 31, D3); below 724 it reads as a list with no header row, plan / As made / struck. Its leading stays constant so a marked row's bold weight moves nothing; rows read in step order under step-group heads.

battery.penWidth: 640px on the Sheet's foot; the 350px log column from 1366
battery.track: 186px desktop / 216px below 724px and in the log column
battery.captionLine: Reserves Clear's height marked or not (24px desktop, 44px narrow touch, two caption lines at wide touch) so picking moves nothing.
battery.clearance: 12px between a desktop axis stop and the core/declared hairline, carried as the declared column's own padding-left rather than a column gap.
battery.appSkin: In .notebook-log the battery takes the App skin (sketch 011 decision 29, 2026-10-02): colour, radius and rule colour only. Picked fills are app blue's text companion; joined stops and segments take the 10px radius at their outer ends; fields and rules read the divider colour.
battery.purpose: The record pen's own instrument: six axes in one grid with the defects, a 1px hairline at the two-thirds line, two group cues heading the columns in the cue face. A genuinely different DOM shape below 724px and from 1366 (stacked groups), not a media-scoped layout.

shell.barHeight: 57px (44px controls, 6px above and below, 1px hairline), sticky from 724
shell.flyout: Fixed from the bar's foot to the window's foot at 224px, 724 to 1589, over a scrim; Escape, scrim, menu button, a chosen place or a width cut close it.
shell.stacking: page, page notice (3), scrim (4), fly-out (5), Import error panel (6), bar (11); pinned by shell.test.js
shell.purpose: Every route renders inside one shell that paints the App ground once; the two Sheet frames paint their own paper over it.

scope.implementedCatalogue: Two contexts, both built. Sheet: Recipe Sheet, ingredient table, Instructions, graduated rules, pen foot, the Sheet's Notebook-form hand (as-made grams, Instructions changes) and the printed log. App: the shell, Home, the Notebook band and version column, History and the upright list, the batch log and its record pen skin.
scope.approvedAppDirection: Option B destination palette with the revised Ingredients green and the preview neutrals (2026-09-21), the five text companions and the filled action (Mark, 2026-10-05, as built), one 10px control radius and active place weight 600 (sketch 011 decision 38, 2026-10-04), the hand. No recipe-specific colors. Unresolved: feedback treatments, pale tints, pressed and disabled states, whether the ink ring is the App's focus colour (app blue is the link colour, approved 2026-10-05), the companions on the subtle surface (about 4.1:1, never decided), the pen's Save weight, motion.
scope.tonalRamps: The Sheet colours carry preview ramps; the App colours carry none. Ramps are preview metadata only; not approved UI colors.
scope.emptyShadowsAndMotion: Motion is empty because none is built (--app-duration is declared and no rule reads it). Shadows lists the App's one shadow, the fly-out's, and its scrim.
scope.appRadius: One App radius, 10px (--app-radius-control), on the App's interactive elements and the surfaces they sit on; marks keep 3px (sprinkle) and 4px (row mark, defect square), History's marks are circles. The Sheet is square and has no radius token.

components.description: Sheet catalogue. Anything counted that the maker types: hairline ink border, no fill, pen blue text in the grotesk with tabular numerals, its own 1.35 leading and a 26px floor so an empty date input cannot collapse on WebKit. Sized to what it holds — a date at 128px, a short figure at 56px with its unit word beside the box as a sibling. 16px and 44px wherever the pointer is coarse.

components.description: Sheet catalogue. The maker's words editing in place as the printed paragraph: no border at rest, pen blue text face, note leading, a hairline vertical inset and a one-line minimum extent, growing with its text. A blank named field carries a hairline baseline. Narrow and coarse-pointer contexts raise it to the shared 44px touch floor and 16px text.

components.name: Graduated rule
components.description: Sheet catalogue. One figure as a printed scale: hatched target band, tick at the value, deviation in words. A focusable button; focus outlines it and marks contributing rows.

components.name: Target chip
components.description: Sheet catalogue. A typed target on a method step. Hairline ink border, no fill, never a control.

components.name: Instructions step
components.description: Sheet catalogue. Step number in a fixed margin column; bold lead-in and prose in the text face; targets as chips; purpose and aside in italic.
components.html:
1. 2

    Gum slurry — the only high-heat step. Toss 1.68 g of the gum blend with ~12 g of the sucrose. Whisk into 120 g of the milk in a small saucepan. Heat, whisking constantly, then pull off.

    temp85 °Chold2 min

    At 120 g this is a thin layer in the pan. It scorches and evaporates faster than a larger volume would.

components.name: Axis mark
components.description: Sheet catalogue. The tasting battery’s per-axis control: a caption line (axis name, inline state, right-aligned Clear), five joined stops on a 186px track, three anchor words in italic. The drawn box is a label with an invisible native radio stretched over it, so the browser’s grouped-radio keyboard semantics do all the work. A picked stop fills pen blue; adjacent stops share one hairline through a negative margin and the picked cell lifts above its neighbours. The caption line reserves Clear’s height marked or not, so picking moves nothing.

components.name: Segmented control
components.description: Sheet catalogue. The battery’s three-way control: a role="radiogroup" of native radios restyled, adjacent options sharing one hairline. Its caption line is the component’s own head, with Clear as the last child. Picking is final — a joined group is a radio, and Clear is the only way back. The picked option fills pen blue; never bold, never underlined.

components.name: Defect toggle
components.description: Sheet catalogue. An independent on/off, so it is a square and a word rather than a filled box: a 13px ink square before the word, filled pen blue when pressed, aria-pressed carrying the fact. The button itself never changes colour. Defects are grid items of the axes’ own grid, in two labelled groups, so the vertical hairline spans them too.

components.name: Text toggle
components.description: Sheet catalogue. An independent on/off recorded in prose, so it is a square and a word like the defect: a 13px leading square before the word, hollow at rest, filled pen blue when on, aria-pressed carrying the fact. The underline stays hairline whether on or off — the square carries the state, the word never bolds and never gains an outline (one fill for every on state, 2026-09-16). Show changes no longer uses it: since 03.5-15 it is an underlined word that names its state, Hide changes while shown, with no aria-pressed.

components.name: Authored block
components.description: Sheet catalogue. The maker's own notes that head the Instructions under a Before you start region name, closed off from the steps by a graduation rule (03.5, D-06).
components.html:
Before you start

  • Taste the Graza straight. Polyphenols degrade with light and oxygen, and the squeeze bottle offers less protection than dark glass. An old bottle at 40 g will disappear entirely.
  • Check the cream’s actual butterfat. The carton states a 36% minimum, which is a floor.

components.name: Fold head
components.description: Sketch 011 decisions 18, 19, 34 A and 41, built in Phase 03.5 (FoldRow.jsx). One full-row button per fold on the recipe route, laid out from the left: the label, Show or Hide as an underlined word, then a dot and an optional count or date. aria-expanded carries the state; 44px floor at every pointer. Every fold head is this component; a Show/Hide is never hand-built.

components.name: App filled action
components.description: Approved 2026-10-05, as built (Home .home__action and Notebook .notebook-action, both weight 600 since 2026-10-05). The App's primary action: app blue's text companion as the fill, the App ground as the label, 10px radius, 44px floor. An accent is never a fill under a white label (app blue reads 3.90:1 there; the companion reads 4.55:1). The pen's filled Save declares no weight and computes 400, an open question for Mark. Hover thickens the border to a whole 2px and the padding gives up the same, so the box never changes size.

narrative.overview:
The cookbook remains the material reference for Recipe Sheets and batch/tasting logs. Around those Sheet surfaces, Sprinkles has a colorful app interface for navigation, recipe context, history, and supporting tools. The two contexts belong to one product: the Sheet supports reading, making, and recording; the app interface supports finding, choosing, and continuing work. The retired name “Sprinkles Jar” is not an interface label.

**The two contexts are named.** The **Sheet** is the Recipe Sheet, the batch and tasting log, and the print sheet. The **App** is Home, Notebook, Recipe Book, Idea log, Ingredients, and Kitchen. Every colour token carries its context as a prefix: `sheet-*` for the Sheet, `app-*` for the App. Earlier drafts of this document named the Sheet after its material.

**The Context Boundary Rule.** Apply Sheet rules to Recipe Sheets, batch/tasting logs, and print, not to every element on a recipe route. Recipe-level name and description, History, provenance, version selection, and navigation belong to app context. Sheet title, Sheet description, ingredients, Before you start, and Instructions belong to the version's Recipe Sheet. On screen, the batch and tasting record is App context (Mark, 2026-09-23); the Sheet in its Notebook form carries only the batch in view's as-made grams and Instructions changes in the hand, and the printed batch log keeps the paper and pen treatment. The Sheet has two forms — Notebook (as-made and log) and Recipe Book (neither) — per `.impeccable/surfaces/route-recipe.md` § "03.5 revision". A shared route does not imply a shared visual context.

Home composition belongs in its surface brief. Mockups are exploration evidence, not token specifications: photographs, handwriting, slogans, and exact component geometry are not approved merely because they appear in a preferred concept.
keyCharacteristics: Two explicit visual contexts: the colorful app interface, and the Sheet (Recipe Sheets and records).
Four implemented Sheet color roles, plus the App's destination colors, text companions and neutrals, all implemented; no recipe-specific colors.
Sheet prose uses the text face; measured quantities use the grotesk with tabular numerals. The App is one grotesk, with the hand for the maker's words.
Sheet controls preserve the binder's ink outlines, pen-blue selection, and distinct focus indication.
Across both contexts, color never carries a verdict; meaning and interaction state remain legible without color.
Approved direction is distinct from shipped components and unresolved visual choices.

rules.name: The Context Boundary Rule
rules.body: Apply Sheet rules to Recipe Sheets, batch/tasting logs, and print, not to every element on a recipe route. Recipe-level name and description, History, provenance, version selection, and navigation belong to app context. Sheet title, Sheet description, ingredients, Before you start, and Instructions belong to the version's Recipe Sheet. On screen, the batch and tasting record is App context (Mark, 2026-09-23); the Sheet in its Notebook form carries only the batch in view's as-made grams and Instructions changes in the hand, and the printed batch log keeps the paper and pen treatment. The Sheet has two forms — Notebook (as-made and log) and Recipe Book (neither) — per `.impeccable/surfaces/route-recipe.md` § "03.5 revision". A shared route does not imply a shared visual context.

rules.name: The Two-Ink Rule
rules.body: Within the Sheet, printed matter is ink black; recorded matter is pen blue; the two never mix on one element. A value that is half plan and half record is two values.

rules.name: The No-Verdict Rule
rules.body: No colour anywhere carries pass, fail, warning, or uncertainty. A figure's standing against its band is stated in words beside the figure; estimated or unreviewed data says so as a word in the Data column; a malformed measurement is a sentence under the field and `aria-invalid`, never a red line. A picked control's pen-blue fill is not a verdict — it is the record's own ink saying *the maker chose this*.

rules.name: The Bookcloth Rule
rules.body: In the Sheet, bookcloth names regions or draws the existing band-sub-row hairline. This role does not constrain green or other identity colors in the app interface.

rules.name: The Counted-in-Grotesk Rule
rules.body: Any value that can be weighed, measured, or compared sits in the grotesk with tabular numerals. Prose sits in the text face.

rules.name: The Lowercase-Unit Rule
rules.body: Units keep their case everywhere, including inside uppercase running heads.

rules.name: The Placeholder Rule
rules.body: A placeholder is an example in ink small print, italic — never a default, never pen blue. A blank field still saves as blank.

rules.name: The Hand Rule
rules.body: In the App, what the maker observed is written in the hand, in sheet pen blue: a tasting's note and problems, a Next time, a Why, a note on a batch, an idea. What the maker specified (ingredients, method, quantities, dates, names) is set in type, because a specification is not an observation. What the app writes is set in type, always, so the hand never speaks in the app's voice and a machine suggestion is never mistaken for the maker's judgement. A question the maker typed to an expert is set in type; it is the maker's, but it is not an observation. The hand is a face, not a colour rule: it is always pen blue, but pen blue is not always the hand. The hand is for display, never entry (sketch 011 decision 17, Mark, 2026-09-27: "type in the prose and show in the hand"): the maker types an observation in the prose-field role — the text face in sheet pen blue, 16px under a coarse pointer — and the saved words show in the hand. No field, textarea or select is ever set in the hand.

rules.name: The Hand Rule on the Sheet
rules.body: (bent per D-19, Mark, 2026-09-24). The Sheet's one exception: batch edits written on the Sheet in its Notebook form — the batch in view's weighed as-made grams and its Instructions changes — are written in the hand, where the rule above would set a weighed figure in type. They are what the maker did at the bench, entered against the printed plan, so they take the pen's voice once recorded; like every entry, they are typed in the field's own type (the display-only rule above). The Sheet's hand is its own rule (`.sheet-hand`): Caveat at `--size-hand-min` with `--sheet-leading-hand` (1), in sheet pen blue, falling back to the text face in italic under forced colours and in print. The plan beside it stays in type and ink; the Two-Ink Rule still holds. Nothing else on the Sheet moves into the hand.

rules.name: The Caption-and-Helper Rule
rules.body: A caption is uppercase and labels exactly one input. A sentence that explains rather than labels is a *helper*, sentence-cased, and it sits beside the caption as a sibling — never folded into it, where `text-transform` would shout it.

rules.name: The 16px Field Rule
rules.body: Wherever the pointer is coarse, `.ink-field` and `.prose-field` read at the note size (16px). Below 16px iOS Safari zooms the page on field focus, which moves the record under the maker's thumb; the app's earlier 13px touch size is retired.

rules.name: The Derived-Cut Rule
rules.body: A cut is never picked: measure each part's content limits, set a value for each, set which part gives way first, and the cut falls out as a sum. When a new part joins the route, it gets measured and ranked, and the sums are redone.

rules.name: The Grouping Rule
rules.body: Layout changes share a cut wherever the set values allow, so the page changes a few times, all at once, rather than one part at a time (Mark, 2026-09-26): at 724 the list-form table, the 20px margin, the stacked band, the bottom tab row and the scrolling header move together; the Sheet's second column, the log's place and the folds' default have a cut each. Touch sizes follow the pointer only — a narrow mouse window keeps mouse sizes — which retired the width arm of the touch union below.

rules.name: The Caption Rule
rules.body: Every caption that sits atop its own content — field captions, axis names, segmented captions — carries one 6px gap (`--gap-xs`) to it, whatever it captions. One rule for every caption site.

rules.name: The Drawn-For Rule
rules.body: A rule governs only the case it was drawn for. The old touch union also matched every narrow width, where a 44px caption line was drawn and verified; applying the wide-touch reserve across the union silently overwrote that drawing at 680, 580, 480 and 393. When a new case appears, it gets its own condition — never a widened old one.

rules.name: The Capability Rule
rules.body: Touch *sizes* read the pointer. Touch *layouts* read the width. A height can grow anywhere safely; a track width cannot, because no layout has been drawn for touch-sized stops at desktop widths.

rules.name: The Sheet-Is-Flat Rule
rules.body: Within a Recipe Sheet or the printed batch log, nothing floats above the paper (on screen the log is App context, which is built flat apart from the fly-out). If an element needs to stand apart, it gets a heavier rule, an ink outline, or the pen's fill — never a shadow.

rules.name: The Focus-Heavier-than-State Rule
rules.body: One focus rule at the browser's own `:focus-visible` boundary draws a 2px ink outline offset 2px — heavier than the 1px outline any pointed-at content carries, and a different sign from a pressed control's fill. A focused element that is also stateful reads both. There is exactly one documented exception: `.is-landing-focus:focus`, a plain `:focus` rule that makes the fork's landing focus visible after a mouse-driven Save, which Chrome's modality tracking would otherwise leave ringless.

rules.name: The Strike Rule
rules.body: A strike means not in force, and what sits beside it says why: beside a skipped step, the word "skipped" (the batch layer); beside a superseded value, its replacement; beside a removed row or step, the word "removed". The stroke is one weight, 1.2px in ink (`--rule-strike`), the same in all three, and it is never the only carrier. Beside means adjacent: next to the replacement, or directly under it, as the ingredient table's struck figure stands under the current one from 724 and in the phone's list (sketch 011 decision 31); a struck paragraph (a changed step's prose, the headnote) stands below its replacement. A struck step's strike is scoped to its prose span so the label beside it stays legible. No builder adds a fourth meaning. (Recorded here from `.impeccable/surfaces/route-recipe-version.md` § 7 and the built `.struck-value`, `.prose-struck-beneath` and `.method-step__prose--struck`, as that brief asked.)

rules.name: The Hover-Is-Weight Rule
rules.body: Hover thickens a border from 1px to a whole 2px and removes exactly that much padding, so the box never changes size — 1.5px renders as 1px at DPR 1, which is why hover needs its own token rather than borrowing the baseline. A joined control thickens in place and stacks above its neighbours. Weight, never position or hue.

rules.name: The One Head Rule
rules.body: A Show/Hide is never hand-built; two drawings of one control contradict each other. - **Upright list** (`UprightRail.jsx`): the vertical row both History (below 1366) and the batch list use — a 12px round mark, a title (meta size, a blue underlined link; bold ink and no underline on the row in view) over a label-size meta line in secondary text, a row at least 44px tall, and a 1px connector that runs only between marks, from just below one mark to the top of the next row and never across a circle (G-03.5-5).

dos: **Do** establish whether an element belongs to app context, a Recipe Sheet, a batch/tasting log, or print before applying visual rules.
**Do** preserve the implemented Sheet tokens; add app tokens only when their roles and values have been specified and implemented.
**Do** keep recipe identity and app accents distinct from ink that communicates plan and actual records.
**Do** keep keyboard focus discernible from selected state, preserve semantic controls, and make touch targets usable.
**Do** state balance, uncertainty, errors, and provenance in words; color never supplies a verdict.
**Do** keep units correctly cased, quantities legible, and required/error feedback attached to its control.
**Do** use the Sheet catalogue for Sheet typography, outlines, pen selection, step order, and print behavior.
**Do** distinguish approved direction, observed implementation, and unresolved design choices.
**Do** keep page composition in surface briefs and reusable visual rules in this document.

**Do** set the maker's saved observations in the hand and sheet pen blue in the App (typed in the prose-field role, never in the hand), at or above the hand's minimum size, with the text-face fallback in place for forced colours and print.
**Do** set a destination's name, count or link in its text companion and its mark in its accent, and fill a primary App action with app blue's companion under a white label.
**Do** give every App control the one 10px radius, every App action a 44px floor, and let hover change a border's weight, never the box's size.
donts: **Don't** impose the Sheet palette's four colors on Home, navigation, recipe context, History, Ingredients, Kitchen, or consultations.
**Don't** extend the Sheet's flatness, square corners, no-motion treatment, or image restrictions into app-wide bans.
**Don't** add shadows, gradients, rounded cards, or animation inside the Sheet merely because the surrounding app can use a different treatment.
**Don't** introduce app palette values, fonts, shadows, radii, or motion timings from exploratory mocks without a design decision.
**Don't** treat sidecar tonal-ramp previews as approved additional colors.
**Don't** use color to encode success, failure, warning, or uncertainty, or make interaction state depend on color alone.
**Don't** paint recipe-level metadata as recorded pen content merely because it shares a route with the Sheet.
**Don't** call the surrounding interface “Sprinkles Jar.” Use the approved section names and vocabulary.
**Don't** put a specification, a label, a date, a heading, or anything the app wrote in the hand, and don't load the hand's file from a network.
**Don't** give a recipe a colour of its own, and don't let a rail, a sprinkle, or an underline mean anything but the place a thing lives or the place you are.
**Don't** use an accent as text or as a fill under a white label (app blue reads 3.90:1 there), and don't fill a picked App control in pen blue: pen blue in the App is the maker's own words.
